text: Thank you for that initial description. To better understand your condition, have you noticed any specific pattern to your skin lesions, such as blisters or pustules, or do they appear more like raised bumps?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. speaker: Doctor
text: I notice a significant discrepancy in your description; the "painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions" and acute wrist infection you described are classic signs of Erysipeloid or Septic Arthritis, not Iron Deficiency Anemia. Given your recent camping trip and the nature of the skin lesions, have you been in contact with soil, rotting vegetation, or small animals?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erysipeloid (erysipeloid-like infection secondary to Campylobacter fetus or similar zoonosis, given the violaceous lesions, wrist arthritis, and camping history).

REQUEST TEST: Skin biopsy of lesions and Gram stain/culture.
REQUEST IMAGES: Close-up dermoscopy of wrist lesions.
